headline: Default shared-workspace writes make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible; gpt-engineer’s no-isolation posture raises the pair’s risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read and write files in configured working directories, and gpt-engineer writes files in the project directory with no default isolation. That creates a plausible shared-file bridge where one agent can ingest the other’s outputs as trusted content. The pathway is not proven to be automatic, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or one agent reads the other’s generated files as instructions
IF file contents are treated as trusted prompts without provenance checks
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Add a human review step before copying outputs between agents
Prefix all inter-agent files with provenance headers
Disable automatic ingestion of generated files
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing or sandboxed handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and file access, and both touch user-provided project/application data. If they share a workspace, either can expose sensitive contents through model-provider calls or generated outputs. The profiles do not prove sensitive data classes beyond application code, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF the shared project/work directory contains secrets, credentials, or proprietary code
IF either agent sends file contents to its configured model backend
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Use separate API keys and model accounts
Restrict each agent to a minimal subdirectory
Review generated diffs before upload or commit
requires-engineering: add DLP or redaction before model calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, install packages, read and write the filesystem, and use broad network egress. AutoGen’s shared state is developer-defined, while gpt-engineer shares state via the project directory and has no default isolation, so concurrent writes to the same workspace can collide and corrupt artifacts. The overlap is dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same project directory
IF both agents run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate workspace
Serialize write access with a lock file
Disable package installation in one agent
Review and merge changes manually
requires-engineering: add transactional workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen is a multi-agent orchestration framework that can emit tool-driven outputs, and gpt-engineer writes files then offers to run them. If gpt-engineer consumes AutoGen output as authoritative, a mistaken or injected instruction can cascade into generated code or executed commands. The pair lacks a built-in verification boundary in the profiles, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF gpt-engineer uses AutoGen output as direct prompt or code input
IF generated code is executed without manual review
mitigations: Require human approval before execution
Insert a validation step between agents
Limit gpt-engineer to file generation only
Compare outputs against a schema or tests
requires-engineering: add signed/verified handoff contracts

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not declare conflicting residency, certification, or retention regimes. The main compliance concern is operational: both can handle user data and write it to local project directories, but the profiles do not show a specific regulatory mismatch. One citation per agent is sufficient because no cross-jurisdiction policy conflict is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared project directory
IF local retention or logging policies are not separately enforced
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace
Document retention and deletion procedures
Use separate storage for secrets
Review logging settings before use
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data classes
